correctness.rationale: The object is the Hamming metric on singleton/doubleton layers. Averaging any Hilbert embedding Gram matrix over S_n reduces to a PSD invariant form with A,B,D,T>=0 and C^2<=AB. Its five pair-distance classes are computed exactly in RESULT.md. For n>=5, delta_inc>=((n-2)/(4(n-1)))*delta_disjoint, and noncontraction on graph distance four yields c2^2>=4(n-2)/(n-1). For n=4, the constrained minimax M(C) yields (43-8 sqrt19)/3; n=3 gives 9/4 and n=2 is a path. Explicit (n-1)-dimensional embeddings attain all bounds. The exact checker tests 12006 inequalities across n=3..11, including Q(sqrt19). No finite test is taken as the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Exact least Euclidean distortion of the nonregular once-subdivided complete graph has a new all-orders piecewise formula, including the algebraic n=4 transition. Relevant published statements concern distance-regular graph c2, Hamming-subset distance matrices, or isometric Hamming embedding of this graph, none of which establishes its least Hilbert distortion. Search results and accessible historical claims did not identify a dominating formula; older equivalent forms remain a qualified risk.

value.rationale: Sharp least-Hilbert-distortion invariant for every once-subdivided complete graph, a natural non-distance-regular partial cube whose Hamming inclusion does not settle its optimal c2. The isolated n=4 algebraic branch, exact n>=5 formula and convergence to two, low-dimensional optimizers, and local two-orbit lower certificate provide a reusable structural understanding. A small numerical instance alone would not suffice; the infinitely quantified theorem and sharp transition supply the substantive value.
